meta.author: wlynch
meta.body:
Did some more digging here - I don't think the issue is that the controller is being re-informed of objects.

This was based somewhat anecdotally on clusters we ran where automatic probes created TaskRuns, and the cluster locked up after O(thousands) of TaskRuns were created (suspiciously near the ~3000 pod-per-namespace mark documented here - https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/sig-scalability/configs-and-limits/thresholds.md). The leading theory was the # of objects was causing issues with etcd leader election and resulting in the Kubernetes API to be unavailable.
It's entirely possible that these issues were unrelated - I've started subjecting a test cluster to a load test with a minimal TaskRun to try and recreate this.

We're at ~10k TaskRuns with the most noticeable effect being the slow down of `kubectl get` calls (which is expected (taking O(seconds)). I noticed there are several instances of `List` calls that are made in the Task/PipelineRun controllers that might be affected, but nothing too severe so far.

meta.author: wlynch
meta.body:
Poking at the Knative code, it looks like it [asynchronously inspects the events](https://github.com/knative/pkg/blob/a02dcff9ee2694ab9bbc694bddbd95d3aaae615b/vendor/k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue/delaying_queue.go#L177) and sees [whether it is past the requested time](https://github.com/knative/pkg/blob/a02dcff9ee2694ab9bbc694bddbd95d3aaae615b/vendor/k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue/delaying_queue.go#L242) so we're primarily limited by what [time.Duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#Duration) can support (so don't try to schedule deletion 300 years in the future and we should be good 😅)

In the case of reconciler failure / crash / restart, my understanding is that everything will be resynced. This will cause the Watcher to go through the same checks to verify if we should delete or reenqueue again. It should be safe to call the same key multiple times.

Yeah I can file an issue. 

Funny enough, embedding status info is why these queries are being done in the first place - it's a mechanism to prevent double scheduling if a Run resource is interrupted without the status info being written back (i.e. query for things with the parent label, if it already exists use that, else create what is missing).
We might be able to avoid some of the query lookups with some journaling, but this will likely expose us to different complexity (I'm primarily worried about name collisions). 😬

meta.author: wlynch
meta.body:
Yes it is! I should update the commit message to reflect why we're making this change.

Before we were updating the Record on every reconcile event - this was fine because we were generally only reconciling on object updates which required us to update the Record. Now that we're doing retries of "not ready to be deleted yet" objects, we need to make sure we only update the Record when we need to, since doing extra updates will push the grace period window since we calculate the grace period w.r.t. to the Record last update time. 

This change just checks if there's a diff in the Record, and only updates if there's data that needs to be changed.

Even if we change this to be more pipeline resource specific (e.g. use .status.completionTime instead of the Record last update time), I think we still want something like this in place to avoid making duplicate write calls for data we know is identical.

meta.author: wlynch
meta.body:
Yes. See https://pkg.go.dev/sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/reconcile#Reconciler

[knative/pkg follows similar behavior](https://github.com/knative/pkg/blob/87426b54db6f1200e2cb9086055fdf7fe90307dc/controller/controller.go#L395), requiring you to wrap the error in [NewPermanentError](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/knative/pkg/controller#NewPermanentError) to stop the key from being re-enqueued.
